Below is a floor plan of the plane you are in. Familiarize yourself with the location of the exits.
Note particularly the exits nearest you. Study how they are opened and also the protective position
you should assume during an emergency landing. When leaving, move to the exits immediately.
Do not go back for coats, purses, or other personal items.
A WORD ABOUT YOUR SEAT BELT-Rough air (turbulence) at high altitudes, although
infrequent, can be severe. When the seat belt sign is lighted in-flight, please comply with the sign
to prevent possible injury. Seasoned air travelers usually leave their seat belts fastened all the
time and pull them up snug whenever the seat belt sign is lighted.

HOW TO USE THE OXYGEN MASK
Jet aircraft fly at high altitude and the cabin is pressurized for your comfort. If cabin
pressure ever
was lost, you would be breathing high altitude "thin" air... so it is
imperative that cigars and cigarettes be extinguished immediately and oxygen masks
be put on as shown below.
WHAT TO DO IN CASE
AN EMERGENCY WATER LANDING IS NECESSARY
1. No smoking. Put out cigarettes and close cover on
ash tray. Adjust your seat back to upright position.
2. Remove high heeled shoes and all cumbersome,
restrictive clothing. Loosen your collar and tie. Re-
move things that obviously could hurt you, such as
glasses and false teeth; sharp objects such as pens,
pencils and brooches.
3. Put on your life vest. It is stowed under your seat.
Do not inflate life vest inside airplane.
4. Sit down and fasten your seat belt. Pull it up good
and tight; this is important. Locate the emergency
exits nearest you.
5. A short time before landing your Captain will issue
a "Brace for Ditching" order. Then, those in forward
facing seats clasp hands under knees and lean for-
ward with shoulders on lap and head down. Those in
aft facing seats clasp hands behind head with shoul-
ders well back. These positions will reduce the shock
of sudden deceleration.
6. After all forward motion has stopped, not before,
unfasten your seat belt and proceed immediately to
nearest exit. Your crew will direct you to rafts.
DO NOT INFLATE VEST INSIDE THE AIRPLANE

1. WHERE TO LOCATE
MASKS.
Oxygen Masks are
located in compartments directly
over each passenger seat. If
cabin pressure is ever lost, com-
partment doors will open auto-
matically and present masks.
Take nearest mask firmly in hand
and pull it from its holder. This
turns on the oxygen.
2. HOW TO USE MASKS.
Remove the plastic bag, coiled
oxygen tube and head band
stored inside the mask. The
mask should then be promptly
placed over nose and mouth.
The oxygen supply tube is long
enough to permit you to relax
comfortably in your seat.
3. HOW
ADJUST
MASKS FOR
COMFORT.
Once mask is in position, it may
be easily adjusted for comfort-
able fit. If too tight, hold mask
in
position and pull gently on
elastic head band with free hand.
If too loose, pull tabs located
where head band connects to
mask. Do not overtighten, as
this may misshape mask and
cause discomfort.
